transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

Water pooling under the salad drawers in a fridge-freezer is almost always caused by a blocked defrost drain. During its automatic defrost cycle, water that should run down a channel at the back of the fridge gets trapped because the exit hole is clogged with food particles or gunk, so it spills over into the cabinet. Before we look at anything else, please check this:
1. Locate the small drain hole at the bottom of the rear wall inside the main fridge compartment (usually under a plastic cover).
2. Check if it looks blocked by debris or ice.
3. If you can safely do so, try clearing it gently with warm water (using a turkey baster or squeezy bottle) and a soft pipe cleaner to ensure the path is open. Let me know: was the drain hole blocked? Is it clear now after cleaning? And did the water stop appearing for a day or two?
ok ill have a look. theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall and its got bits of lettuce and gunk in it. i'll clear it out with a cotton bud and some warm water, is that ok?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, that is perfectly fine. A cotton bud works well for the initial gunk, but if there's a deeper blockage in the tube below, you might need to flush it with a bit more warm water (a turkey baster or small jug) to ensure the path all the way down is open. Please let me know: did that clear the drain properly? And once you've done this and put everything back, has any new water appeared in the bottom of the fridge?

ok done, i unplugged it and cleared the hole with the cotton bud and warm water. the water went straight down it this time and theres been no more pooling over the next few days, seems sorted. water was only ever inside the fridge, nowhere near the plug btw

That is excellent news. It sounds like the blockage has been fully cleared and your fridge is back to normal operation. To help stop this happening again in a few months, just try to keep that drain hole clear of food scraps when you are tidying up, and avoid placing items directly against the rear wall where they might trap moisture or debris. If it starts pooling again, you now know exactly what to check first. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
